core_obligations: The first two assertions (proof lines 1575-1585): the author bounds the number of increasing sequences of subobjects of a fixed cardinality index by transfinite induction, using that an increasing sequence eventually stabilises, which gives the cardinality bound on the set of subobjects.

The third assertion (proof lines 1586-1590): to each subobject the author assigns the subset of morphisms from the generator that factor through it, shows that two subobjects are equal exactly when the assigned subsets are equal, and concludes that the number of subobjects is bounded by the cardinality of the power set of the set of morphisms from the generator.
proof_roadmap: Bound increasing sequences of subobjects by transfinite induction.
Encode each subobject by the set of morphisms from the generator factoring through it.
Use that the encoding is injective to bound the number of subobjects by a power set.
difficulty_reason: The lemma gives bounds on the set of subobjects of an object of an abelian category with a generator, in terms of the cardinality of the set of morphisms from the generator (statement lines 1558-1573). The proof is a complete argument: the stabilisation of increasing sequences of subobjects is used to bound their number by transfinite induction (proof lines 1575-1585), and each subobject is encoded by the set of morphisms from the generator factoring through it, an injective encoding, which bounds the number of subobjects by a power set (proof lines 1586-1590). The non-formal content is the encoding of subobjects by sets of morphisms. The claim is H2.
